title: Dirac's theorem: 4-chromatic graphs contain a $K_4$-subdivision
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph whose chromatic number equals $4$. Then $G$ contains a subdivision of $K_4$: there are four distinct branch vertices joined pairwise by six paths that are internally disjoint from one another and internally avoid all four branch vertices.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
the chromatic number of G equals 4
replaced:
(Dirac, 1952). \emph{If \texttt{G} is 4-chromatic, then \texttt{G} contains a
subdivision of \texttt{K$_{4}$}} --- the case \texttt{k = 4} of Haj\'os' conjecture.
